memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle. Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide, with two projections set parallel to each other. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way. Make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle and make forty silver bases to go under them — two bases for each frame, one under each projection." - Exodus 26:15-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Beneath the curtains stood the structure — upright frames of acacia wood, each one standing on two solid silver bases. The beautiful coverings would have collapsed in a heap without these. Every frame stood upright because it rested on a foundation that held it steady.

Notice that no frame stood alone. Each had its own bases, and each stood shoulder to shoulder with the others, forming a wall. Together they held up the whole dwelling. Individually a frame is just a plank of wood; joined and grounded, it becomes part of a structure that houses the glory of God.

This is a picture of what God is building with His people. Peter writes that we are living stones being built into a spiritual house (1 Pet 2:5), and Paul says the church is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the chief cornerstone (Eph 2:20-22). Your stability does not come from your own strength but from the foundation you rest on. And your purpose is not merely personal — you are part of something God is assembling. Stand firm on Christ, stand close to His people, and let Him build.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What foundation am I actually resting my life on?
Do I see myself as part of what God is building, not just an individual believer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are building something greater than any of us alone. Ground me firmly on Christ, and let me stand faithfully alongside Your people as part of Your house. Amen.
